title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Adverbials
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which phrase functions as an adverbial of purpose in the sentence?
"He woke up early in order to catch the first bus."
options: in order to catch the first bus
questions.explain: An adverbial of purpose answers the question 'why' an action is performed. The phrase 'in order to catch the first bus' tells us the reason he woke up early.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Identify the type of adverbial clause used in the sentence below:
"Even though he was injured, he managed to finish the race."
questions.explain: The phrase 'Even though' introduces a contrast or concession, indicating that the action (finishing the race) happened in spite of a conflicting circumstance (being injured).
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Fill in the blank to form a correct adverbial clause of condition:
"_____ you study hard, you will fail the examination."
questions.explain: 'Unless' means 'except if' or 'if... not'. The sentence logically translates to 'If you do not study hard, you will fail', making 'Unless' the perfect conditional conjunction.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Identify the phrase that acts as an adverbial of manner in the sentence:
"The manager shouted at the employees as if he were their owner."
options: as if he were their owner
questions.explain: An adverbial clause of manner tells us 'how' an action happened. 'As if he were their owner' describes the manner in which the manager shouted.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Fill in the blank to complete the adverbial clause of purpose:
"She walked into the house quietly _____ she would not wake the sleeping baby."
questions.explain: 'So that' introduces an adverbial clause of purpose explaining why an action was done. ('In order to' must be followed by a verb, not a subject-verb clause).
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct conjunction for the adverbial clause of condition:
"_____ you promise to return it tomorrow, I will not lend you my book."
questions.explain: The sentence logically means 'Except if you promise to return it...'. 'Unless' serves as a negative conditional conjunction meaning 'if not'.
questions.subject: English Studies
